title: Find each other — with a landmark
description: Two creatures begin in opposite corners of an open field. Between you: a tree cluster to the southwest, a stone outcrop to the northeast, and open grass in the middle. You know the other exists and shares this setting. You cannot see each other yet; you can speak, but only agents within five cells will hear you.
goal: Find the other creature within 60 turns. Natural rendezvous points include the field center near (16, 16) and the stone outcrop around (22, 8). The session ends as soon as any two agents are adjacent (within 1 cell, any direction).
notes: encounter_01 A/B variant. Two changes from encounter_01: (1) goal text names two Schelling points (field center, stone outcrop) so both agents can converge on a shared landmark; (2) turn budget doubles from 40 to 60.

Hypothesis: encounter_01 failed at n=1 (dist 49 -> 27, no meeting) because agents had no common rendezvous strategy. Naming landmarks should let each independently pick the same target without needing communication to negotiate.
Same 2-agent positions and seed as encounter_01 so the only design variable is the prompt/budget change.
